title: 2.3 Natural and Human Induced Climate Change
description: Milankovitch cycles, solar output, volcanic aerosols, land use change and greenhouse gas emissions. Easy level.

questions.question: What are the three external causes of climate change?
options: Changes in solar radiation, atmospheric composition and land surface
They are interdependent, so a change in one place leads to changes elsewhere
Rising air temperature warms oceans, which then fuel stronger storms
Changes in atmospheric composition, land use and solar radiation
questions.correctAnswer: Changes in solar radiation, atmospheric composition and land surface

questions.question: What are internal causes of climate change?
options: Ocean and atmosphere circulation that redistributes energy
By adding greenhouse gases and aerosols to the atmosphere
Orbital variations help initiate glacial and interglacial periods
Altered reflectivity changes the amount of solar energy absorbed
questions.correctAnswer: Ocean and atmosphere circulation that redistributes energy

questions.question: Who proposed the theory linking climate to variations in Earth orbit?
In which decade was the Milankovitch theory proposed?
Which set of movements makes up the Milankovitch cycles?
options: Sulfuric acid haze reflects incoming sunlight
They prevent sunlight from reaching the ground
The wobbling of Earth axis of rotation

questions.question: About how often do sunspot numbers reach a maximum?
What is a sunspot?
options: Changes in the shape of Earth orbit around the Sun
Urban surfaces and haze alter the local energy balance
A cooler, darker magnetic storm region on the Sun
By adding greenhouse gases and aerosols to the atmosphere
questions.correctAnswer: A cooler, darker magnetic storm region on the Sun
